title: Capacity-aware metric synthesis for inference ops
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a pragmatic working doc to define a compact set of telemetry signals and tracing anchors for capacity-aware inference operations. The goal: produce a small, actionable metric set and trace conventions that let SREs and pod owners reliably answer three questions within 5–15 minutes during incidents:
  1) Is the problem capacity (GPU) or software (queue/packing/kv cache)?
  2) Which tenant(s) or model(s) are the primary contributors?
  3) What mitigation (scale, fallback, throttle) will regain health quickly?

Audience:
  - Observability engineers implementing backend instrumentation
  - Serving/runtime owners (serving-runtime, infra teams)
  - Oncall SREs and L2 operator runbooks
  - Product managers evaluating SLOs for model-serving tiers

Design constraints and principles (notes to self):
  - Keep per-node telemetry light: prefer cardinality-reduced tags and computed derived metrics over freeform labels.
  - Prioritize metrics that map to action (scale up, pin model variant, enable cached responses).
  - Support tenant-weighting for fair SLO application across multi-tenant pools.
  - Favor percentiles (P50/P90/P95/P99) with explicit windowing (1m, 5m, 1h) for dashboards and alerts.
  - Tracing should be sparing but dense enough for root-cause (adaptive sampling + severity-weighting).

Signal inventory (synthesized):
  - node.cpu_util_pct: gauge, node-level, 10s scrape, 0-100.
  - gpu.util_pct: gauge, per-gpu, 10s scrape.
  - pool.alloc_capacity: gauge, logical capacity units in pool (reserved + available).
  - pool.headroom_pct: derived = available_capacity / total_capacity * 100, 10s.
  - request.inflight_count: gauge, per-node and per-pool.
  - request.queue_length: gauge, per-worker-process.
  - request.batch_size: histogram, record per-response. Buckets: 1,2,4,8,16,32,64.
  - request.latency_ms: histogram, end-to-end for generation API (token emission loop included).
  - request.latency_token_ms: derived = latency_ms / tokens_emitted (approx per-token cost signal).
  - kv_cache.hit_rate_pct: derived, per-model-per-pool, rolling 5m.
  - prefix_reuse_pct: derived, fraction of requests that matched prefix cache.
  - tenant.weighted_p95_latency_ms: derived using tenant weight (see below).
  - model.token_cost_usd: derived, per-model token cost over rolling 1h.
  - scheduler.pack_efficiency_pct: derived, measured as tokens_processed / theoretical_max_tokens_given_GPU.

Metric definitions and collection notes:
  - request.latency_ms: captures from request received at front-door to final payload flush. Tagging: route, model, model_variant, region, tenant_id (low-cardinality hashed), sample_id. Do not add prompt text or user-provided metadata.
  - kv_cache.hit_rate_pct: numerator = number of requests where kv_cache_lookup==HIT and cache_age < TTL. Denominator = total lookups. Roll up to per-model per-pool to avoid noise.
  - tenant.weighted_p95_latency_ms: each tenant is assigned a weight equal to max(1, sqrt(tenant_30d_qps)). Use a weighted percentile algorithm in the metrics backend. This avoids tiny noisy tenants dominating alerts.

Trace anchor and span naming conventions (compact and stable):
  - Root span: service=\"inference-front\" name=\"inference.request\" attributes: {tenant_hash, route, model=string, model_variant=string, request_id}.
  - child span: name=\"scheduler.pack\" attrs: {pack_id, batch_size, pack_efficiency_pct}.
  - child span: name=\"runtime.infer\" attrs: {gpu_id, kernel_variant, seq_len, kv_cache_hit: bool}.
  - child span: name=\"kv.lookup\" attrs: {prefix_key_hash, hit: bool, age_ms}.
  - fallback span: name=\"fallback.model_call\" attrs: {from_model, to_model, reason}.
  - span durations: capture wall-clock and CPU/GPU time separately where feasible (instrument runtime to emit gpu_exec_ms).

Trace sampling strategy (practical):
  - Always sample errors (status != OK) and high-latency tail traces (latency > P95 for model+route).
  - Base sampling: 0.5% of steady-state requests across public pools.
  - Adaptive uplift: if pool_headroom_pct < 20% or pack_efficiency drops > 30% vs baseline, raise sampling to 5% for 15 minutes.
  - Severity weighting: tag traces with severity {info, warn, error} and preserve error traces longer in retention tier.

Dashboard composition and panel guidance (investigation-first layout):
  Top row: global health + hot indicators (single-pane glance)
    - cluster capacity matrix: total_capacity / used_capacity per-region per-pool (heatmap).
    - global headroom_pct (1m, 5m trend sparkline).
    - rolling cost burn (1h).

  Middle row: throughput & contention (resource-level)
    - per-node GPU util histogram (P50/P90/P99).
    - request.queue_length over time by worker (stacked small multiples).
    - pack_size distribution heatmap (x-axis pack_size, y-axis latency bucket).

  Bottom row: model/tenant breakout (drillable)
    - tenant-weighted P95 latency (top-20 tenants) with weight and raw qps.
    - kv cache hit rate per-model (sparkline + current value).
    - per-model token cost USD with simple 1h trend.

Panel UX notes:
  - Provide a single-click filter to narrow to pool->node->model. Persist the filter across panels.
  - Show population count next to percentiles (e.g., P95 (n=3.2k)). If n < 50, show a caution tint.
  - For cost panels, annotate unusual value spikes with links to trace/bookmark (if available).

Alerting guidance (alert only on actionability):
  - Avoid pure percentile alerts on raw latency. Instead combine conditions: tenant_weighted_p95_latency > threshold AND pool_headroom_pct < 30% for 5m.
  - Alert severity examples:
    - Sev3: pool_headroom_pct < 20% for 10m (operator action: scale or divert traffic).
    - Sev2: tenant_weighted_p95_latency > target (depends on tier) AND pack_efficiency_pct < 50% for 5m (investigate packing regressions).
    - Sev1: sustained gpu.util_pct > 95% on >50% of nodes for 10m (auto-evacuate/abort flows + paging).

Sampling and cardinality playbook (ops heuristics):
  - Hash tenant_id to 4 buckets for dashboards that must show per-tenant slices; keep original tenant_id only in traces.
  - For model labels, normalize names (remove commit hashes) and expose model_family tags for rollups.
  - Use derived metrics (ratios) to reduce labels: e.g., prefix_reuse_pct instead of storing prefix_key per-request.

Migration plan (minimal safe rollout):
  1) Implement metric collectors on one non-production pool; expose dashboards in staging.
  2) Run adaptive sampling in shadow mode for 48–72 hours to validate targets and volume.
  3) Gradual rollout to 25% of production pools, observe cardinality and query costs.
  4) Tune sampling and cardinality knobs, then full rollout.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
  - Dashboards render under 2s for typical queries (1h window).
  - Alerts fire in staging simulating low-headroom (test harness) and map to documented runbook steps.
  - End-to-end trace capture for induced regressions (packing bug) available in trace UI and links back to the failing request in the dashboard.
  - Query cost for telemetry remains <= 6% of overall monitoring budget (QPM/ingest volume check).

Open questions / discussion points:
  - Tenant weighting: is sqrt(QPS) the right function or use 90th-percentile demand? (Marco to A/B test).
  - How to expose pack_efficiency so it is actionable to product (need runtime counters).
  - Retention tiers: how long do we keep error traces vs baseline traces? Budget tradeoffs.

Next steps and owners:
  - instrument runtime to emit pack_id and pack_efficiency_pct (owner: Jonah, due: 2024-12-05).
  - implement tenant weighting algorithm in metrics backend (owner: Marco, PR referenced above).
  - prototype dashboard layout in staging and run operator tabletop (owner: Sana, runbook draft by 2024-12-15).

Notes to self (scratch):
  - keep labels minimal; prefer rollups.
  - test cold-cache vs kv-cache burst separately (cold starts can mimic capacity issues).
